execution.progress: extract and inspect take one round; sowing is two paid one-round phases whose work, reserved seeds and patch persist; resume pays only the remaining phase after rechecks; rooting and growth run only in ordinary simulation.

details.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.2 energy each. extract: target your own whole untreated berry item; one unit per attempt (quantity 1): 1 round, 0.5 energy. inspect: x, y a site in reach and/or target your own item or a sowing patch in reach: 1 round, 0.2 energy. sow: target your seed lot; x, y a site in reach on open ordinary soil (.), moisture 0.3-1.2, waterlogging at most 0.1, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 berry plants or patches being sown within 5 m. 2 rounds of 1 energy: loosen the patch, then place and cover the seeds; a loosened patch left by cancelled work needs only the second. pause, resume (workId), cancel: no energy. Refusals and failed rechecks cost nothing. No tool, vessel, water or soil is supplied.
details.effects: A whole berry unit (0.2 kg, food 8) is crushed: 0.01 kg of seeds (5 %, no food, no ageing) and 0.19 kg of pulp with all its food and age; both keep origin, harvest round and decay. The seeds of one unit are the one propagule the plant rules give one fruit unit; viability is unknown until something emerges. A unit whose parent is not a living berry plant has no represented seed: a paid failure, all pulp. Sowing moves the seeds from your inventory into the patch record, covered 5 mm deep in soil loosened 0.03 m. The patch gains establishment only from actual temperature (none at 6 C or below, full from 20 C), light, soil moisture (full from 0.6) and season; cold, darkness, drought or waterlogging stall it. At 12 a rooted seedling appears with no fruit (stock at most 4, the parent plant interval); fruit grows only under the existing growth rule; anyone may gather it. Watering a rooted plant is rooted-plant-watering. An unworked round pauses; cancel returns unsown seeds once and leaves loosened soil; death leaves them where you died. No reward or refund.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.question: How can I maintain reliable food access without unnecessarily exhausting nearby plants?
evidence: Berry and root meals supplied nutrition in previous eating trials.
At tick 31, extracting one owned berry produced one seed lot and pulp retaining its food value; seed viability remains unknown.
Inspection at tick 35 found ordinary soil at (16,19), moisture 0.65 and six same-food plants within five metres; the site was reported not sowable.
At tick 38 the seed lot remains owned, energy is 40 and health is 100.
value.uncertainty: A suitable site and seed viability remain unestablished. No seedling or new food supply has been produced.
value.goal: Maintain safe food access and test whether propagation can support future shared supplies.
completedSteps: Gathered and ate berry and root meals.
Learned seed propagation and extracted one berry seed lot.
Inspected and rejected the first candidate planting site.
outputs: One owned berry seed lot of unknown viability.
value.missing: A verified suitable planting site, sowing, and observed establishment and fruit production.
value.next: Eat the ageing pulp and inspect (17,23); choose whether to sow from the resulting evidence.
value.benefit: Meals supplied nutrition. Extraction preserved the berry's food value as pulp while separating seeds for a small trial.
